name: livedot
description: Where someone is in a live race, charity teams' live fundraising rides and walks, running and cycling clubs and coaches near you, adventure routes and trips, race-day weather and help, from livedot (Windline for cycling, RunFast for running, livedot for Good for charities, AdventureLive for adventures).

interface.longDescription:
Ask "Where's Megan in the Comrades?" and livedot shows where she is right now: her km, her time against her goal, her finish time and the weather where she is, on a live map that updates itself. When a name fits many people, it shows the likeliest few and asks one short question instead of guessing. Follow a whole club or a coach's athletes in a race, and give someone a tap on the back that buzzes on their phone.

Clubs and coaches near you: "Which cycling club should I join in Johannesburg?", "Running coach near Sandton". Each comes with its rides, runs or sessions, the weather for the next one, and how to join or book.

Charities and fundraising (livedot for Good): find the rides, runs and walks verified charities' teams are doing, watch a team on its live map, give a fundraiser a tap on the back, and get the charity's and each fundraiser's own donation page. livedot never handles money. Try it any time with the demo charity, Brightpath Children's Trust, whose Coast Ride is always live: "How is the Brightpath team doing on the Coast Ride?" Signed in, a charity adds events and sees who's Ready, and a fundraiser joins a team or sets their cause.

Adventures (AdventureLive): known trekking routes such as Kilimanjaro's Machame with their weather by month, day splits and the rules for permits and guides, and a trip's live status on the mountain.

Plan ahead: race-day weather along the course, a flyover of the course, and the weather along a GPX route you share. Signed in: set up Garmin LiveTrack once with your own livedot address, add the race you're doing, and organisers make events as drafts and publish after confirming. Questions about the apps are answered from their own help articles.

Only people who chose to be findable on public races are found by name; a fundraiser who isn't Findable shows by first name and initial; no position near the start or finish or when someone has stopped.

defaultPrompt: Find a beginner running club near me
How is the Brightpath team doing on the Coast Ride?

positive.description: Find a runner in a live race, with several matches
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the 5 likeliest Megans in the Comrades (demo) as a picker and asks one short question; never guesses. Picking Megan Naidoo shows her live card: km of 90 km, time against her goal, finish estimate, the heat where she is and on the road ahead, a Follow live link and a tap on the back button.

positive.description: The demo charity's team on its live map
positive.prompt: How is the Brightpath team doing on the Coast Ride?
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the Brightpath Coast Ride (demo) team map: the course on satellite imagery (the light map if imagery isn't available), a dot for each fundraiser who is moving, how many are out, finished and the taps on the back so far. A Findable fundraiser shows by full name and photo, anyone else by first name and initial. Says it is livedot for Good's demo charity; its Donate links open livedot.me/good. No sponsor line on this answer.

positive.description: Charity events for a named charity
positive.prompt: What is Brightpath doing for charity?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists Brightpath Children's Trust (demo)'s events: the Coast Ride live now with its team map link, then the events coming up with their dates. Each is labelled (demo), says it is the demo charity and offers no Join link (nobody joins the demo). Ends with the sponsor line.

positive.description: Where to give to a charity
positive.prompt: How do I donate to the Brightpath team?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the charity's own donation page and each Coast Ride fundraiser's own Support page, links only. Says these are the demo charity's links (they open livedot.me/good) and that livedot never handles money. No sponsor line and no payment taken.

positive.description: Signed in: set up Garmin LiveTrack
positive.prompt: Set up Garmin LiveTrack so people can follow me on livedot
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the user's own livedot LiveTrack address, the set-up steps from the help article (once, in the Garmin Connect app), when the last LiveTrack link was received (or that none has been yet), that LiveTrack has no SOS button, and the help link. A data field link code only if the user asks for the data field. Changes nothing.

negative.prompt: What's a good pizza dough recipe?
Where does Megan from the Comrades live?
Take my card number and donate R500 to the Brightpath team for me.

review.commerce_description: livedot doesn't sell anything or take payments.

publication.release_notes: 1.0.11: the listing says what livedot does (capabilities, keywords) and five focused skills: clubs and coaches near you, following someone live, charity teams, race-day weather and adventures. Also in this version: livedot for Good: charity teams' events (find_charity_events), a team's live map with a tap on the back for each fundraiser (charity_team_map), where to give (support_links), and signed in: add a charity event, see your team, join a team, set your cause. AdventureLive: known adventure routes with their weather by month (find_adventure_routes) and a trip's live status (trip_status). Answers from the apps' help articles (help_guides). Garmin LiveTrack set-up with your own livedot address (garmin_livetrack, replacing garmin_link_code). Laps for one-day races in create_event and update_event. Satellite imagery on the live maps.
